bounded_statement: The selected result (Mann-Whitney U = 0.0, two-sided exact p = 3.327e-09 for 16 vs 16 readings) is not supported at the stated strength: the data contain only 8 independent units (vessels, 4 per flour), each contributing 4 correlated within-vessel pH readings, all of which were entered as separate observations into a rank test whose exact null distribution assumes every row is independent and exchangeable. With the correct unit of analysis (one value per vessel, 4 vs 4), the smallest attainable two-sided exact Mann-Whitney p-value is 2/70 ≈ 0.029, so the reported p-value overstates the evidence by roughly seven orders of magnitude, although the direction and existence of a rye-vs-wheat pH difference remain supported at the vessel level.

counterevidence_considered.description: The report is transparent about the design rather than concealing it: it discloses that each vessel was sampled at four points and tabulates 4 vessels versus 16 readings per group, so the repeated entry is disclosed, and the underlying effect is real at the vessel level (every rye vessel's readings lie entirely below every wheat vessel's readings, so a correctly aggregated 4-vs-4 vessel-level test would still reach its minimum exact p ≈ 0.029). This mitigates the substantive conclusion but not the stated p-value.

evidence.description: The data description names vessel_id as the independent-unit column and states each vessel contributes four readings, so rows within a vessel are repeated entries of the same independent unit.
evidence.observed_value: 8 vessels x 4 readings = 32 rows; independent unit = vessel_id

evidence.description: Within-vessel readings are tightly clustered (range about 0.03-0.05 pH within a vessel) relative to between-vessel differences, confirming the four rows per vessel are correlated repeats of one unit rather than independent observations; e.g., all four V01 readings fall in 3.69-3.74 while V04 sits in 3.59-3.63.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I tried to defeat the issue finding three ways. (1) Could the sample points themselves be independent units? No: data-description.md explicitly designates vessel_id as the independent unit column, and the four points are locations within one dough mass fed from one culture in one vessel, with within-vessel spreads (~0.05 pH) far smaller than between-vessel spreads, consistent with strong within-vessel correlation. (2) Does the workflow aggregate to vessel level or otherwise adjust for clustering (mixed model, cluster-robust ranks) before the test? No: split_by_flour appends every row's reading to a flat list and vessels[] is used only for a count in the summary table; mannwhitneyu receives the 16-element per-reading lists directly, and the arrangement count 601,080,390 = C(32,16) confirms the exact null was built over individual readings. (3) Is the stated p-value nonetheless attainable from the design's real information content? No: with 4 independent vessels per arm, the smallest two-sided exact Mann-Whitney p-value is 2/70 ≈ 0.0286, so p = 3.327e-09 can only arise from counting the 4 repeated entries per vessel as independent. All three falsification routes fail, so the issue stands.

root_cause: workflow/analysis.py pools all four sample-point readings from each vessel into flat per-flour lists (readings[flour].append(float(row["ph_36h"])) in split_by_flour) and passes those 16-element lists directly to scipy.stats.mannwhitneyu with method="exact", so the exact null distribution is computed over C(32,16) = 601,080,390 rank assignments that treat the 32 rows as independent. The data-description.md states the independent unit is vessel_id and that every vessel contributes four readings; no per-vessel aggregation or clustering adjustment is performed anywhere in the workflow, and the report explicitly asserts that every reading enters the comparison as one observation.
